preconditions.description: The number of vertices in the tree is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n for x, y in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two vertices within the valid range [1, n].
The input contains exactly n-1 edges, forming a tree.
The number of queries is between 1 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v_i <= n and 0 <= d_i <= 10**9 and 1 <= x_i <= 10**9 for v_i, d_i, x_i in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query has a valid vertex v_i in [1, n], distance d_i in [0, 1e9], and value x_i in [1, 1e9].

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n integers, one for each vertex.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= output_values[i] <= m * 10**9 for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: Each vertex's value is non-negative and does not exceed the maximum possible sum of all query values.

postconditions.expression: all(output_values[i] == sum(x_i for v_i, d_i, x_i in queries if i in k_subtree(v_i, d_i)) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: The value of each vertex i is the sum of all x_i from queries where i is in the d_i-subtree of v_i.
